findings.claim: Claim 2(a) of the rev2 submission: 'the first candidate whose bytes verify is served'. The code does not behave that way on the first candidate: _select_candidate returns immediately at rank 1 whenever verification fails (resolver.py:1376-1395, 'if not status: ... / if rank == 1: return location, "unverified_preferred_copy"'), so a readable-but-drifted preferred copy is served WITHOUT consulting the remaining candidates - even when one of them holds the requested bytes and would have verified.
findings.evidence: Temp probe rank1_drift_rank2_ok (3 identical copies, then rewrite only the p10 copy with different bytes; dropbox keeps the requested bytes) run against both trees. HEAD: status=reused_exact, download_required=false, served_path=...\companies\...\2025.pdf, served_claim_sha256=0c753cf6065f693d6fdeecc3132c6848ff1a14dbdc7b404a2ef82742f862197d, served_actual_sha256=2e3c56d1f4554fcccdfacd51c3499566ea5ce2a86ae94968190f479b20ab27a0, verified_copy_available=true, served_is_verified_copy=false, trace ['entity_gate_rejected: 0','2025: unverified_preferred_copy','2025: candidate <loc>:content_sha256_mismatch:2e3c56d1f455','2025: matched']. PRE tree: same drifted copy served, trace ['entity_gate_rejected: 0','2025: matched'] (silent). So the outcome is not a regression, but the claimed ordering rule does not hold and the available verified copy is bypassed.
findings.impact: The byte-verification track - the safety value of segment 3 - is skipped precisely in the case where it can help: the resolver reports REUSED_EXACT (download_required=false) for bytes that fail the document's own content_sha256 while a local copy that passes the check exists in the same source group. A consumer (filing-fetch) is handed the drifted file on the strength of a claim the resolver itself disproved one line earlier.
findings.required_action: Remember the first readable rank-1 candidate and move the claim-trust fallback AFTER the loop (return the remembered copy only when no candidate verified), so 'the first candidate whose bytes verify is served' becomes true and the frozen A-side fixtures still resolve (nothing verifies there). Add a regression case for 'preferred drifted + non-preferred verified -> serve the verified copy'. This is a few-line change in resolver._select_candidate.

findings.claim: The justification recorded for the owner-pending deviation S-10 (owner-scope-decisions-2026-09-12.md section 9; evidence/b02-implementation.md sections 3 and 4): the claim-trust rule for the preferred copy is '严格不宽于 pre-B02' / '这**不宽于** pre-B02 (pre-B02 对首选无条件信任且从不校验字节)'. That bound is false: pre-B02 trusted the PRIORITY-ELECTED row, which can be a row the new qualification track excludes, so rev2 can serve unverified (and provably mismatching) bytes in a case where pre-B02 returned MISSING.
findings.evidence: Temp probe rejections_best_priority_drift: .rejections copy at the best priority (p10) holding the requested bytes, a healthy copy at p30 whose bytes were rewritten, third copy deleted, document forced active. PRE tree: status=missing, matches=0, download_required=true, trace ['entity_gate_rejected: 0','2025: rejections_path']. HEAD (350b67a): status=reused_exact, download_required=false, served_path=...\Dropbox\Stock\2025.pdf, served_claim_sha256=0c753cf6065f693d6fdeecc3132c6848ff1a14dbdc7b404a2ef82742f862197d, served_actual_sha256=c0ee64c0299f5aa568479ec21d0aba080328e5e38119bcd28371c19e04ca8831, trace ['entity_gate_rejected: 0','2025: unverified_preferred_copy','2025: candidate <loc>:content_sha256_mismatch:c0ee64c0299f','2025: matched']. The .rejections-at-best-priority layout is the scanner's own (adapters/dayu.py ticker/filings/.rejections/<id>), so the configuration is production-shaped; the extra condition is only that the surviving qualified copy's bytes drifted after the last scan.
findings.impact: The owner is being asked to approve S-10 on a factual bound that does not hold: the deviation is wider than 'exactly the pre-B02 trust level' because the trusted row is now the highest-priority QUALIFIED row, which may be a row pre-B02 never served (pre-B02 answered MISSING). This is the same class as rev1's P1-01 (bytes that fail the claimed content_sha256 served as reused_exact with download_required=false), and under the run's own L03 acceptance line ('all copies unusable -> unavailable, do not take another revision') the drift case is not covered by the approval request.
findings.required_action: Restate S-10 precisely in owner-scope-decisions section 9 and evidence/b02-implementation.md sections 3/4: the served row is the highest-priority qualified copy of the document's own source group, it may differ from the row pre-B02 would have elected, and it may be served where pre-B02 returned MISSING (with the rejections_best_priority_drift probe as the counter-example). Either add that probe as a regression case or anchor rule (b) to 'the row the pre-B02 election would have served' so the deviation really is bounded by the pre-B02 trust level.

findings.claim: Claim 3 of the submission: 'cancellation is sticky and a cancelled request gets no handle at all'. The cancellation contract is only observed at candidate/charge boundaries; a cancel that lands while the first candidate's bytes are being read is not honoured, and the request still returns a handle.
findings.evidence: Temp probe cancel_mid_request (HEAD): _ReadBudget() injected, resolver._sha256_of_file monkeypatched to call budget.cancel() and then compute the real digest of candidate 1. Result: budget={'candidates': 1, 'bytes_read': 27, 'cancelled': True} and status=reused_exact, match_count=1, download_required=false, trace ['entity_gate_rejected: 0','2025: matched'] - i.e. a handle was returned after the budget was cancelled. The pre-cancelled case (test_r4b02_cancellation_reads_no_byte_and_returns_no_handle) and the sticky-after-a-cancelled-request case (my probe cancel_after_first: second resolve -> missing, trace 'candidate_verification_cancelled') both behave as claimed.
findings.impact: Low safety impact (in the observed window the digest matched, so the returned copy is the requested version) but the documented contract is stronger than the code: an operator aborting a resolve during the digest cannot rely on getting no handle, and no diagnostic records that cancellation arrived late.
findings.required_action: Either check budget.cancelled after _verify_candidate returns and before returning/continuing (one line next to 'if not status:'), or restate claim 3 / the _ReadBudget docstring as 'cancellation is observed at candidate and charge boundaries; a read already in flight completes'.

findings.claim: Claim 2: candidates are 'restricted to the document's own source_id group'. The restriction has no covering test (a mutant that deletes it keeps all 23 cases green), and the code silently drops it when the document's source_id is empty (resolver.py:1352-1362, 'not own_source_id or ...').
findings.evidence: Mutation M6_no_source_group_restriction (replace the candidate filter condition with just item.get('candidate_rank')) on a temp src copy: '23 passed in 1.93s' - no case detects the removal (baseline and M1-M5, M7 all kill the intended test). Behaviour probes: two_groups (SQL surgery) shows the restriction works and matters - with documents.primary_source_id set to a fabricated second source group, HEAD serves that group's copy where PRE served the priority-elected copy of the other group; null_primary (primary_source_id=NULL) shows the bypass: HEAD returns reused_exact with trace ['entity_gate_rejected: 0','2025: unverified_preferred_copy','2025: candidate <loc>:content_sha256_mismatch:0c753cf6065f','2025: matched'] for a document with no declared version. Reachability: scanner.py:975-978 sets source_status='quarantined'/'incomplete' whenever primary is None, and resolve() queries source_statuses=('active',), so no scanner-produced catalog can reach the bypass; it needs another candidate source or a hand-edited catalog.
findings.impact: The one behaviour that makes 'serving the requested version' well defined is unverified by the acceptance file, and the escape hatch is undocumented in the claim and in evidence section 2 (which states the restriction absolutely). A future change could delete the restriction with a fully green suite.
findings.required_action: Add a regression case for the group restriction (the two-group fixture needs SQL surgery because sources.content_sha256 is UNIQUE - it can be marked as a latent/mechanism-level case), and state the 'empty document source_id -> no restriction' bypass explicitly in the S-10 record so the owner sees the full trust path.
